reasons: Both answers are near-equivalent layered designs that reject both proposals for concrete reasons, keep stock and prices live from PostgreSQL, version listing keys by the price batch and stay within Redis/PG/Django. B edges ahead on the must-not-show-false-availability constraint: it uses a safety_stock display threshold, makes a checkout recheck mandatory, and flags that stock data may itself arrive late (for example from 1C), which no cache scheme could fix. A has its own strong points, including fail-closed display on a stock-read timeout and over-fetching IDs for live filtering, but these make a slightly smaller difference.
